title: Desktop Offline Bundle Install Policy
description: Archive/executable extension blocklists and zip-bomb size caps enforced by apps/desktop-client/electron/bundle-verify.ts (M04) when importing an Offline Bundle. Read directly (not via TypeScript source parsing) by apps/portal-api/src/portal_api/routers/admin.py (M02, P15 관리자 설정) so both modules share one contract instead of M02 coupling to M04's source formatting (CLAUDE.md 원칙 2/3).

archive_extensions.description: Lowercase, dot-prefixed archive extensions treated as forbidden nested archives inside an Offline Bundle.

executable_extensions.description: Lowercase, dot-prefixed extensions classified as executable/code and forbidden inside an Offline Bundle.

source_code_exception.description: D-096. The outbound mirror of asset-upload-policy.json's field of the same name, and the ONLY way an executable_extensions entry may survive inside a Bundle. It exists because a stdio MCP server is nothing without its code, while executable_extensions forbids every form that code can take. Three conditions must hold together, and bundle-install.ts enforces all three: (1) the Bundle's own manifest declares an included asset of one of the listed asset_types; (2) the flagged entry sits under THAT asset's own directory, in allowed_subdirectory — code belonging to an mcp_server asset cannot license a .py sitting next to a Knowledge index; (3) its extension is in allowed_extensions, which re-allows readable source only, never compiled or shell forms. Because the Bundle manifest is read before this check, and every file in a Bundle is already covered by checksums.sha256, a file that passes here is one a reviewer could have read and whose bytes are pinned. Archives are never re-allowed — checkNoNestedArchives is untouched by this field.

asset_types.description: included_assets[].asset_type values that can carry code. An asset of any other type never licenses an executable entry.

allowed_extensions.description: Lowercase, dot-prefixed extensions exempted from executable_extensions inside a qualifying asset's directory. Must be a subset of executable_extensions — this field only ever SUBTRACTS from a denial, so reading executable_extensions alone still tells you the worst case.

allowed_subdirectory.description: The single subdirectory, directly under the asset's own directory, where code may live (the bundler writes an asset's uploaded files to `assets/{folder}/{asset_id}/source/`). Anything executable elsewhere in the Bundle — including elsewhere inside the same asset's directory, such as its index/ — still fails.

_why.description: Optional free-text justification, so narrowing/widening this requires updating the stated reasoning.

max_total_uncompressed_bytes.description: Zip-bomb defense: total uncompressed bytes allowed across the whole bundle.

max_single_file_uncompressed_bytes.description: Zip-bomb defense: uncompressed bytes allowed for any single entry.

max_compression_ratio.description: uncompressed/compressed ratio above which an entry is treated as a suspected zip bomb.

min_ratio_check_bytes.description: Entries smaller than this (uncompressed) are exempt from the compression-ratio check.
